Cheonggyecheon and the streets along it (from just south of Jongno, where Jongmyo begins)
the east end of Yulgok-ro and the Sejong-ro side street

enclosure.why: inside the palace wall: the gates, Yeongjegyo, the corridors round Geunjeongjeon and the halls are drawn once you walk in through Gwanghwamun (core/enclosure.js)

n.en: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts

areas.why: the palace site is the real one at 1/4 (about 115 x 264 m); lawn and trees round it

blockers.why: Bosingak's stone base and its side steps

text.en: Joseon's bell pavilion on Jongno. Its bell opened and closed the city gates; now it rings in every New Year with 33 strokes.
text.ko: 종로의 조선 종루. 종을 쳐서 도성의 문을 열고 닫았고, 지금은 해마다 33번 울려 새해를 맞아요.
text.ja: 鍾路にある朝鮮の鐘楼。鐘で都の門を開け閉めし、今は毎年33回ついて新年を迎えます。
text.zh: 钟路上的朝鲜钟楼。钟声曾开关都城城门，如今每年敲33下迎接新年。

landmarks.why: the palace woods along the walls behind the halls (green in summer, red in autumn)

streams.note: Cheonggye Plaza to Hwanghakgyo, about where they are on the 1/4 Seoul map (the real stream runs on about 2 km more to Jungnangcheon). Bridges in their real order and roughly their real spacing: Mojeongyo, Gwangtonggyo, Jangtonggyo, Sewoongyo, Baeogae Bridge by Gwangjang Market, Ogansugyo at Dongdaemun, Hwanghakgyo.
